senses: to fasten, fix, set, especially drive, sink, force in
to compose, make heard or give out
to celebrate, tell of, record, compose accounts of
la:verb:pango.html:
pango, nxi, nctum, and pēgi or pĕpĭgi, pactum (v. Neue, Formenl. 2, 474 sq.), 3, v. a.
root pac-; Sanscr. pāca, band, fetter; Gr. πήγνυμι, fix; πάχνη, frost; πάσσαλος, peg, etc.; cf.: pagus, pagina, paciscor; old form paco, pago; cf.: rem ubipacunt, XII.Tab. ap. ; v. P.
,
to fasten, make fast, fix; to drive in, sink in (syn.: figo, configo).
Lit.: pangere, figere; unde plantae pangi dicuntur, Müll.: clavum,; v. clavus: tonsillam pegi laevo in litore, Pac. ap. Fest. s. v tonsilla, p. 356 Müll.; Col. poët. 10, 252; .—
Transf.
To set, plant any thing: ramulum,: vicena millia malleolorum,: lactucam : taleam olearum,; hence, transf.: filios,to beget children,—
To set or plant any thing with any thing: ipse seram vites pangamque ex ordine colles, (4, 16), 15: vitiaria malleolis,.—
Trop.
Versus carmina or facta (like componere), to make, compose, write, record: hic vostrum panxit maxuma facta patrum, Enn. ap. (Epigr. v. 2 Vahl. p. 162; but the verse: horrida Romuleum certamina pango duellum, is spurious): carmina,: versus de rerum naturā,: aliquid Sophocleum,: ἀνέκδοτα, : poëmata,: chartas,: pangendi facultas,; : de pangendo nihil fieri potest,.—
In gen., to make: neque prima per artem temptamenta tui pepigi,.—
To fix, settle, determine, agree upon, agree, covenant, conclude, stipulate, contract (class., but only in the perf. forms; for the pres. and fut. pacisci was used; v. : paciscor facit et pepigi et pactus sum, Serv. ad. ; cf.: paciscor, stipulor, despondeo): ducentis Philippis rem pepigi,: pactam rem habeto,: terminos, quos Socrates pepigerit (al. pegerit),: fines,.—With ne: si quis pepigerit ne illo (medicamento) usquam postea uteretur,; so : pacem nobiscum pepigistis, ut, etc.,: inducias pepigisse,: non fuit armillas tanti pepigisse Sabinas,: resumere libertatem occultis insidiis pepigerant,: cui pretium pepigerat,. —Freq. of a marriage contract, to promise, engage, pledge, etc.: habeon' pactam (Sororem)? ; : quod pepigere viri, pepigerunt ante parentes,: te peto quam lecto pepigit Venus aurea nostro,: haec mihi se pepigit; pater hanc tibi,.
la:verb:pango.inflection: nxi, nctum, and pēgi or pĕpĭgi, pactum, 3, v. a.

la:noun:panis.html:
pānis, is, m. (
neutr. collat. form pāne, is, Plaut. ap. , and and 114 P.; v.infra; cf. also: non item apud vos est positum hoc pane et hic panis? etc.,.—In gen. plur., panium, acc. to Caes. ap. and 114 P.; panuin, acc. to P.) [from the root pa, to feed; whence also πάομαι, pabulum, and pasco], bread, a loaf.
Lit.: tunc farinam aquā sparsit et assiduā tractatione perdomuit finxitque panem, etc.,: a pistore panem petimus, vinum ex oenopolio,: haec sunt ventris stabilimenta: pane et arsā bubulā, etc.,: quin tu rogas, Purpureum panem an puniceum soleam ego esse,: sordidus,: panis rubidus,: cibarius panis, coarse bread (v. cibarius), : secundus,black bread,: ater,: durus ac sordidus,: siccus,dry bread,: panis plebeius, siligneus,; cf.: panis tener et niveus mollique siligine factus,: vetus aut nauticus,: lapidosus,: fermentatus,: azymus,: subcinericus,: oleatus,: mollia panis, the crumb, Plin.

13, 12, 26, § 82: panis crusta,the crust,: bucella panis,a mouthful,: mucida caerulei panis consumere frusta,.—

In partic., a loaf: comesse panem tres pedes latum potes,: bini panes,: ex hoc effectos panes, jaciebant, etc.,: panes et opsonia,: panes quos coxerat tradidit,: tortam panis unius,: quinque panes,: cum esuriente panem suum dividere,: frange esurienti panem tuum,.—Hence,
Transf.
Food in general: non in solo pane vivit homo,; ; and trop. of food for the soul, spiritual nourishment: ego sum panis vitae,the food which gives life,; , etc.—
A mass in the shape of a loaf, a loaf: panes aeris,: aut panes viridantis aphronitri,.

la:noun:Pan.html:
Pān, Pānŏs (acc. Pāna), m., = Πάν,
Pan, the god of the woods and of shepherds, the son of Mercury and Penelope, ; : Pan erat armenti custos, Pan numen equarum,: Panos de more Lycaei,. He was represented under the form of a goat; hence, semicaper Pan,; cf. . His mistress, Syrinx, was transformed, at her request, by the nymphs into a thicket of reeds, from which Pan made the shepherd's pipe (σύριγξ), ; . He is also said to have fallen in love with Luna, and to have gained her favor by the present of a ram, Serv. In war he was regarded as the producer of sudden, groundless (panic) terrors, sqq.—He was called at a later period the god of All (τὸ πᾶν), .—
In plur.: Panes,gods of the woods and fields resembling Pan,; .—Gen. Panum, Mela, 3, 9, 6.—Acc. Panas, Col. poët. 10, 427.
